findings.title: Placeholder-chat skills sentinel not scoped per session
findings.problem: The migration effect and handleSetSelectedSkills both key pending skills on the single global chatSkillsKey('') sentinel. startNewChat() never clears or re-scopes this key, so it is shared by every not-yet-created chat for a user.
findings.impact: Picking skills on placeholder chat A, navigating away without creating it, then opening a new placeholder chat B and creating B migrates A's skills onto B — a chat the user never associated them with. Reachable via a single tab (abandon-and-reopen) or two tabs open concurrently for the same user.
findings.recommendation: Scope the pending-skills sentinel per placeholder session (e.g. a token set by startNewChat and cleared/rotated on each call), or clear chatSkillsKey('') inside startNewChat() before a new placeholder begins.

findings.title: saveChatSkills never deletes the key when skills are cleared
findings.problem: saveChatSkills(userId, chatId, skills) returns early without touching storage when skills.length === 0, so clearing a chat's selected skills to [] leaves the previously-persisted entry (including chatSkillsKey('')) in place.
findings.impact: A stale '' sentinel entry can survive a clear and be picked up by the reload effect's migration, attaching an old, discarded skill selection to the next real chat created — the same class of unintended cross-chat leak as CR-001, rooted in the shared helper this fix's migration step now depends on.
findings.recommendation: In saveChatSkills, when skills.length === 0, remove the key (storage.remove(userId, chatSkillsKey(chatId))) instead of returning without effect.
